Contributed to provide a translation for a work that previously had no English translation in the corpus.

div.p: The Riddle of the Number Three. Drink thrice, or as many times three: such is the mystic law, whether for one who drinks three, or for one who multiplies three by three, to weave the cube from nine uneven threes. The right of three is the same as that of thrice three: all things are in these — the form of a begun human being and the completion of a full birth; and that end of fate which holds the last of nine times nine. Three brothers, begotten of Ops; three sisters, born in order, of the female sex — Vesta, Ceres, and Juno. Hence Jove's thunderbolts are three-forked, hence Cerberus, hence the trident, and the threefold egg of Helen with her brothers. Thrice the new purple filled the spindles of Nestor, and the crow, three times more long-lived than that age; whom, gathering the generations in nine triple courses, the bronze-footed stags surpass three times Nestor's span, three of whose ages the bird of Phoebus (the raven) outlives, whom nine times older the bird of the Ganges goes before — the bird whose temples are radiant in their cinnamon nest (the Phoenix). Threefold is Hecate, three the faces of the maiden Diana; three the Graces, three the Fates, threefold the voice, threefold the elements, three the Sirens in Trinacria; all things by threes: three winged ones, three half-goddesses, three half-girls, bidden, three times three, to contend with the Muses for the palm, singing with mouth, hand, breath, with the boxwood pipe, with the lyre-string, with the voice. Three the parts of philosophy, three the Punic wars, three-month the turns of the years and of the sky, and through the shadow of night the threefold watches; thrice the late sentinel, when Mars is caught, sings the bright signs of the coming dawn. And he who, conceived in the evening of a tripled night (Hercules), fixed four times three rich spoils to his trophies. And the lyric bards are of the number of the Memnosynes (Muses), three of whom alone the right hand of Phoebus once held; but Cithaeron three times consecrated three of them in bronze, by the religion of the fathers, who feared to have scorned the six. The triple three-night festivals were celebrated in the Tarentine games, such as the triennial rites at Thebes for twice-born Bacchus. The first three battles of the Thracian gladiators, in three wars in order, the sons of Junius sent as offerings to their father's tomb. She too (the Sphinx), seeking marriages through three riddles — what was two-footed and four-footed and three-footed, all alone — terrified Aonia: a bird, a lion, a three-formed maiden — the Sphinx, with the wings of a bird, the feet of a beast, the face of a girl. Three partnerships gleam in the Tarpeian temple. Three kinds of arts make human dwellings: he who lays the stones for the walls, he who lays the beams on the roof, and he who adorns the plastering with the final touch. Hence the cask of Bromius (wine-measure) and hence the Sicilian medimnus: the practice of measuring unfolds the one by three, the other by twice three. In physics, three first things: God, the world, the form given; a triple of all kinds — begetter, begettress, begotten. Through three kinds of triangles the rule runs: equilateral, or with equal legs, or unequal in all. The perfect number coalesces into three parts, so that the same, by the assembled triple, is dissolved through thrice three. Three, the first, has an even, an odd, and a middle; but it alone, as it divides three, so also divides five and seven; and, set in the whole number under the point of the centre, it marks off the solid thirds as the cube proceeds, sundering the equal parts from the odd by its triple; and a triple middle is in even numbers, when of four and six and twice four the same navel (omphalos) is distinguished. Threefold law, which the four times three Tables (the Twelve Tables) ratified: the sacred, the private, and that which is the common property of the people anywhere. A triple kind of interdicts: "from which I shall have been driven by force," or "in which of two places it shall have been," or "of whose goods." Threefold liberty, and threefold the diminution of civil status. Threefold the kind of speaking: the sublime, the moderate, and that of a slender thread. Threefold too the manner of healing, whose names are by reason, or by method, or by experience; and medicine is threefold: to preserve, to prevent, to cure. Three the cultivations of the orators: that which Rhodes, ruled by its Colossus, and you, Attic Athens, loved; and that which prose of Asia drew from the stages to the stern benches, imitating in lawsuits the numbers of the choruses. Hence the tripods of Orpheus, because they are three — earth, water, flame. A triple consideration for the stars: position, distance, form. And music, both the measure and the mother of melodies, is threefold: mingled in books, secret in the stars, made common in the theatres. Martial Rome is threefold: in cavalry, plebs, and senate; by this number the tribes, and the tribunes of the sacred mount. Three squadrons of the knights, three names of the nobler sort. Three are the names for the lyre-strings, three the names for the month. The Geryons are threefold, threefold the framing of the Chimaera; Scylla is threefold, made of three — dog, maiden, fish. The Gorgons and the Harpalycae and the Furies are in a band of three; and the three prophetic Sibyls, of a common name, whose fatal songs are three books, which the cultivation of thrice five men preserves. Drink thrice. Three is the number above all things; three is the one God. Here too, lest the game run by with an inert number, let it have ten times three threes and ten times nine.
